title: Resolve counts-only conflicts via element-wise MAX, not unconditional ours
context: When a hard merge conflict is confined to the grounding counts sentence, the old strategy (keep ours unconditionally) silently discarded whichever side carried a higher count. A higher count can be the ahead-of-store signal that fnd_6391b4242f depends on — a branch claiming a record its store never received. Unconditionally discarding it masked the signal and misclassified the merged doc as 'lagging' instead of 'ahead'. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: Resolve counts-only conflicts by taking the element-wise MAX of ours and theirs per field (decisions, bugs, constraints, components, policies), rather than picking the whole line from one side. If one side carries a phantom/uncommitted count, it survives into the resolution and the merged doc correctly classifies as 'ahead' against the true store.
consequences: Phantom counts (ahead-of-store signals) are now preserved across merges instead of silently discarded
Each count field is independently maximized, not just whichever whole line is numerically bigger
Requires element-wise max computation and unified rendering via renderCountsMatch() to keep generator and merge driver in sync
Post-merge healing by hunch grounding --refresh still works; merged state is guaranteed >= max(ours, theirs) per field
Adds regression test coverage for per-field max and the phantom-count scenario from davesheffer's reproduction
alternatives_rejected: Unconditionally keep ours (old approach) — silently loses higher counts and ahead-of-store signals
Pick whichever whole line is numerically higher — misses cases where different fields are higher on different sides
Leave conflicts unresolved for humans to decide — burdens users with deciding every counts-only conflict
